drivingQuestion: In what case do the first tanna and Others dispute liability?
outcomeNote: The dispute is framed as the meaning of 'yes', with baraita support for 'stay where you are'.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁבָּאוּ לִתְבּוֹעַ שְׂכָרָן מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וּנְגָחָן שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת וּנְשָׁכָן כַּלְבּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וָמֵת – פָּטוּר. אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: רַשָּׁאִין פּוֹעֲלִין לִתְבּוֹעַ שְׂכָרָן מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת.
segments.en: § «The Sages taught:» With regard to salaried «laborers who came» into their employer’s courtyard «to claim their wages from the homeowner, and the homeowner’s ox gored them, or the homeowner’s dog bit them, and» a laborer «died,» the homeowner is «exempt. Others say» that he is liable, as salaried «laborers are allowed» to enter their employer’s property «to claim their wages from the homeowner.»

segments.he: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דִּשְׁכִיחַ בְּמָתָא – מַאי טַעְמָא דַּאֲחֵרִים? אִי דִּשְׁכִיחַ בַּבַּיִת – מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What are the circumstances? If» the employer «can be found in the city, what is the reason of the others,» who hold him liable? The laborers could have met him in the city to claim their wages and did not need to enter his courtyard. «If he can be found» only «at home, what is the reason of the first tanna,» who exempts him? Clearly they are entitled to claim their wages.

segments.he: לָא צְרִיכָא, בְּגַבְרָא דִּשְׁכִיחַ וְלָא שְׁכִיחַ, וְקָרֵי אַבָּבָא וַאֲמַר לְהוּ ״אִין״; מַר סָבַר: ״אִין״ – ״עוּל תָּא״ מַשְׁמַע. וּמַר סָבַר: ״אִין״ – ״קוּם אַדּוּכְתָּךְ״ מַשְׁמַע.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «No,» these are not the circumstances under discussion. This halakha is «necessary» only «with regard to a man who can» sometimes «be found» in town «and» sometimes «cannot be found» in town, «and» the laborers «called» to him «at the gate» of his courtyard, «and he said to them: Yes.» One «Sage,» referred to as the others, «holds» that the term «yes» in this context «indicates: Come in.» Therefore, he is liable for their death. «And» one «Sage,» the first tanna, «holds» that the term «yes» in this context «indicates: Stand in your place» and I will come out to you. Since he did not give them permission to enter, he is exempt.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר ״אִין״ – ״קוּם אַדּוּכְתָּךְ״ מַשְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא: פּוֹעֵל שֶׁנִּכְנַס לִתְבּוֹעַ שְׂכָרוֹ מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת, וּנְגָחוֹ שׁוֹרוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אוֹ נְשָׁכוֹ כַּלְבּוֹ, פָּטוּר – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּכְנַס בִּרְשׁוּת. אַמַּאי פָּטוּר? אֶלָּא לָאו דְּקָרֵי אַבָּבָא, וְאָמַר לֵיהּ ״אִין״, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ ״אִין״ – ״קוּם אַדּוּכְתָּךְ״ מַשְׁמַע.
segments.en: «It is taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion of «the one who says» that «yes» in this context «indicates: Stand in your place. As it is taught» in a baraita: With regard to a salaried «laborer who entered» his employer’s courtyard «to claim his wages from the homeowner, and the homeowner’s ox gored him, or his dog bit him,» the homeowner «is exempt, although» the laborer «entered with permission.» The Gemara asks: «Why» is he «exempt» if the laborer entered with permission? «Rather, is it not» because it is a case «where» the laborer «called» him «at the gate, and» he «said to him: Yes? Conclude from it» that «yes» in this context «indicates: Stand in your place.»
